answer: Each identity anchors to one registered truffle orchard: inoculated oaks on a named parcel, filed under one key, harvest log checked yearly. One orchard, one identity; a second claim fails, a dead orchard voids it; no harbor shelters a duplicate. A fake costs 7,500 units to plant, plus 1,825 days before the first truffle ripens at its zenith. Cheapest cheat: buy a stranger's bearing orchard, 3,000 units, but the seller surrenders their identity, rooted trees can't move, and a forged deed fails the registry, sending a ripple to every later claim. 100 fakes cost 750,000 units and 182,500 days.
